question: An AC generator works on the principle of :

options.text: force on a current carrying conductor

solution:
The correct answer is **'__electromagnetic induction__'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• AC generators work on the **principle of Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction**, which states that electromotive force – **EMF or voltage **– is generated in **a current-carrying conductor that cuts a uniform magnetic field**.
 
• This can either be achieved by rotating a conducting coil in a static magnetic field or rotating the magnetic field containing the stationary conductor.
 
• The preferred arrangement is to **keep the coil stationary **because it is easier to draw induced alternating current from a stationary armature coil than from a rotating coil.
 
• **The generated EMF depends on the number of armature coil turns, magnetic field strength, and the speed of the rotating field.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__****AC generator:**

 
• AC generator is a machine that c**onverts mechanical energy into electrical energy.**
 
• The AC Generator’s **input supply is mechanical energy **supplied by steam turbines, gas turbines and combustion engines.
 
• The** output is alternating electrical power in the form of alternating voltage and current.**
